Subject: Intermittent blackhole after on-prem route-stitch (logs attached)

Karthik / Redwood team,

We started a phased handoff of the on-prem edge this morning (cut 1 of 3) and are seeing intermittent blackholing for a subset of flows coming over the new transit. Symptoms: 2-3 minute loss of application traffic every ~30 minutes from a small set of customer subnets. The traffic returns without obvious config changes.

Observed so far: traceroutes from our app tier to Redwood ingress show TTL expiry / no reply at the handoff hop occasionally. We captured a sample trace and a packet capture; attaching a condensed trace below and the full trace as handoff-trace-20270612.txt.

Sample traceroute (condensed):
  1 10.10.1.1 1.2 ms
  2 10.20.1.1 2.0 ms
  3 172.31.254.1 3.4 ms  <-- handoff device
  4 * * *
  5 * * *
  6 52.14.200.45 10.2 ms

We suspect either a transient routing loop / route-stitch issue at the transit handoff or an egress SNAT state exhaustion on your side. No changes were made to ACLs on our edge during the window.

Attachments: handoff-trace-20270612.txt, handshake-diagram-annotated.png

Requested: can you validate the route advertisement at your handoff (next-hop, AS path, communities) and share your route-table snapshot for the affected session? Happy to hop on a call if useful.

- Priya Raj
NetOps Lead, Acme Corporation (acme-noc@acme-corp.com)

Thanks Priya and team — I reviewed the sample trace and the annotated handshake diagram. A couple of initial hypotheses and quick checks below.

Initial takeaways:
- The pattern of intermittent *complete* non-response at a single hop often points to either (A) an overlay/local routing engine that briefly rejects/blackholes for a set of flows (e.g., next-hop churn), or (B) an MTU/fragmentation mismatch combined with stateful middlebox behavior resulting in packets being dropped mid-path.
- The condensed traceroute shows the handoff device at 172.31.254.1 consistently, so it's almost certainly local to the transit handoff rather than deep in our fabric.

What we will check on our side (immediate):
1) Verify if our eBGP session with the transit advertises the same next-hop and whether route reflector policies are causing periodic withdrawal (Marcus).
2) Confirm conntrack table sizes and SNAT ephemeral port usage on the handoff instance; if ports are exhausted we'll see spikes of failure for some flows (Neha).
3) Check for MTU mismatch on the GRE/IPSEC encapsulation at the on-prem appliance; if fragments are being dropped some devices will drop instead of fragmenting (Marissa).

Actions / mutual action plan (proposed):
- Acme: provide one example source IP and the exact prefix announced for that traffic. Also, please confirm whether you see any RPM/ACL denies at the handoff device during the blackhole interval.
- Redwood: we'll increase conntrack logging for 2 hours and capture a high-frequency tcpdump on the handoff interface; we'll also snapshot BGP state every 30s for a 3-hour window.
- Joint: if logs point to SNAT exhaustion we'll coordinate a temporary increase in port pools or a NAT-device reboot during a low-impact window.

Can we align on a 2-hour window today at 17:00 PT for synchronous captures? If not, give a preferred time and we'll make it work.

Attachments: route-table-snapshot.json (from our edge control plane)

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Network Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks — we can do the synchronous capture. Confirming details:
- Example source IP (redacted in paste): 198.51.100.47
- Affected prefix: 198.51.100.0/24
- Handoff device log snippet during the last blackhole window (we've attached a fuller syslog in handoff-trace-20270612.txt):
  Jun 15 09:26:18 handoff-01 kernel: conntrack: table full, dropping packet for src=198.51.100.47 dst=52.14.200.45 sport=443 dport=49152 proto=TCP

We can also see occasional path MTU errors in the capture (ICMP frag-needed responses) that line up with the blackhole timestamps. Suspect a combination of conntrack exhaustion + an MTU path where an intermediary is not allowing fragmentation.

We'll be on the 17:00 PT capture window and will enable verbose conntrack logging; we will also temporarily expand ephemeral port ranges if the first capture indicates exhaustion.

Priya Raj
